mathematical_checks: Equal-PSR full-Bernoulli oracle value is exactly E=A Phi(C/A)+(1-A) Phi(C/(1-A)), by minimizing the common null probability at a=A.

For A=m<=1/2, p=2m r is an admissible symmetric submodel. The three-outcome thinning construction has KL exactly 2m KL(r||s), and merging inactive/failure outcomes gives the claimed Bernoulli KL upper bound.
For A>1/2, complementing probabilities changes both B and C signs; the even lambda restores q=A+B lambda(C/m) cos(x). The same q is globally physical.
The explicit uniform null proves V<=2m Phi(C/m) without a minimax exchange. Positive second term of E proves V<2E for C nonzero.
Writing t=m/(1-m), u=|C|/m gives R=2/[1+Phi(tu)/(t Phi(u))] with the stated coefficients.
Positive-series normalization yields u d/du [Phi(tu)/Phi(u)]=Cov(2N,t^(2N))<=0 for u<1. Continuity suffices at u=1; no finite boundary moment is assumed.
Phi(t)/t is nondecreasing, hence G(m) is nonincreasing and the uniform mean-neighborhood bound follows. G approaches one at the symmetric mean.
The extended opposite-sign physical null has the same PSR lower bound, by convexity and the displayed ordered-probability gradient.
C=0, A endpoints, and |C|=m are treated separately; no undefined V/E or zero-times-infinite lambda is used.
The factor-two sharpness family is strictly physical for 0<epsilon<1. For fixed epsilon, the nonleading Bernoulli terms are O_epsilon(A^2), so the stated J/E inner limit holds.

The positive series bounds the Taylor remainder by v^4/[12(1-v^2)]. It gives g/f~sqrt(2) epsilon^(3/4) and the exact rational expression tending to two. Sequential parameter selection establishes sharpness without assuming an inner limit for V/E.

The pure-PSR counterexample has full information log(2) per query, whereas paired-beta and its continuous-prior pairing Rao-Blackwellization have asymptotic rate log(2)/2; a fixed finite odds-grid RB rate is strictly smaller.
